Wrap your UI in `AssistantRuntimeProvider` with a runtime (for example `useLocalRuntime(...)`). See Pick a Runtime. ### Viewport & Auto-Scroll `Viewport` is the scrollable container. It auto-scrolls to the bottom as new content streams in, but only if the user hasn't scrolled up manually. Expanding a disclosure inside a message, such as a collapsible tool call card (a control with `aria-expanded="false"` that opens no popup, or the `` of a closed `
`), pauses it so the card stays where the user opened it; other clicks, text selection and keystrokes keep following, and scrolling back to the bottom or using `ThreadPrimitive.ScrollToBottom` resumes it. A new run or a thread switch also ends the pause. Set `autoScroll={false}` to disable this entirely. ` {/* messages */} ` ### Turn Anchor By default, new messages appear at the bottom and scroll down. With `turnAnchor="top"`, the user's message anchors to the top of the viewport. The question stays at the top and the response streams in below it. ` {/* messages */} ` When `turnAnchor="top"` is set, `MessagePrimitive.Root` registers the latest assistant message as the top-anchor target and the preceding user message as the anchor, so no additional component is required. The viewport itself manages a stable reserve element that provides the missing scroll range while the assistant response grows. This is the behavior used by the Thread component by default. Use `topAnchorMessageClamp` to control how much of a long user message remains visible when `turnAnchor="top"`. Messages up to `tallerThan` stay fully visible. For messages taller than that, `visibleHeight` controls how much of the message's bottom edge remains visible above the assistant response: ` {/* messages */} ` ### Viewport Scroll Options `ThreadPrimitive.Viewport` has three event-specific scroll controls: * `scrollToBottomOnRunStart` (default `true`): scrolls when `thread.runStart` fires; it has no effect with `turnAnchor="top"` * `scrollToBottomOnInitialize` (default `true`): scrolls when the thread's messages first load * `scrollToBottomOnThreadSwitch` (default `true`): scrolls when `threads.selectionChanged` fires These work alongside `autoScroll`. If `autoScroll` is omitted, it defaults to `true` for `turnAnchor="bottom"` and `false` for `turnAnchor="top"`. ` {({ message }) => { if (message.role === "user") return ; return ; }} ` ### ViewportFooter `ViewportFooter` registers its height so the auto-scroll system accounts for it. It does not position itself; add `sticky bottom-0` to keep it at the bottom of the viewport.
